Hammer tapping like a rhythm only he knows,
Sawdust falling like a soft brown rain,
Building dreams on someone else’s name.
Cuzzie bros down below yelling “she’ll be right,”
Tin roof ringing in the morning light,
He just grins with a coffee in his hand,
Says “one more wall and we’ll call it a plan…”
Chilly bin rattles in the back of the ute,
Cold ones waiting like a quiet salute,
Work boots worn but they carry him far,
From backyard builds to a half-built star.
Friday rolls and the sky turns gold,
Stories get bigger, the beers get cold,
He laughs too loud but you don’t mind,
There’s a kind of freedom in his kind…
Oh Jeffy B, still swinging free,
Somewhere between the man and the dream,
Riding that road like he’s chasing time,
With a crooked grin and a busted rhyme…
Jeffy B… yeah he’ll always be,
Half wild heart, half family tree.
Late night riding with the wind out wide,
Thinks he’s faster than the thoughts inside,
Moonlight dancing on a chrome machine,
Somewhere between who he is and who he’s been.
Says he’ll settle, yeah maybe one day,
But there’s always one more job, one more pay,
And the world keeps turning like his old key,
And somehow… it keeps on needing Jeffy B.
